sanskrit: anu sūryam ud ayatāṃ hṛddyoto harimā ca te | yo rohitasya gor varṇas tena tvā pari dadhmasi ||
english: Let your heart-glow and your jaundice rise up following the sun. With the colour of the red cow we envelop you round about.

sanskrit: pari tvā rohitair varṇair dīrghāyutvāya dadhmasi | yathā tvam arapā aso atho 'harito bhava ||
english: With red colours we envelop you round about for long life, so that you may be free of disease — be free of jaundice!

sanskrit: yā rohiṇīr devapatyā gāvo yā rohiṇīr uta | rūpaṃrūpaṃ vayovayas tena tvā pari dadhmasi ||
english: The red cows that belong to the gods, and those that are red — with form upon form, with life-force upon life-force, with these we envelop you round about.

sanskrit: śukeṣu te harimāṇaṃ prapaṇākāsu dadhmasi | atho hāridraveṣu te harimāṇaṃ ni dadhmasi ||
english: Into parrots we transfer your jaundice; into the yellow-plumed birds we transfer it; and likewise into the turmeric-yellow plants we deposit your jaundice.

sanskrit: yāḥ purastād ācaranti nīcaiḥ sūryād atho divaḥ | etam apsarasāṃ vrātaṃ brahmaṇācchā vadāmasi ||
english: Those who roam about in front, below the sun and below the sky — this troop of Apsarases we address with the sacred formula.

sanskrit: yā adharād ācaranti jihmā mukhā karikratīḥ | āhatā apa tā ito naśyantv ataś cinvatīḥ ||
english: Those who roam about below, with twisted faces, raving in their deeds — beaten off, let them vanish from here, those who pick up things from this place.

sanskrit: yāḥ kulyā yā vanyā yā u conmādayiṣṇavaḥ | sarvās tā mṛśmaśākaraṃ dṛṣadā khalvām̐ iva ||
english: Those who haunt streams, those who haunt forests, and those who indeed drive men to madness — all of them I grind away like barley in a mill with a grinding stone.

sanskrit: cetantīm aśmalāṃ palāṃ tāsāṃ vo namo arciṣe | ārād yakṣmaṃ ni dhatta- -asmān no adhi pūruṣāt ||
english: To the conscious Aśmalā, to Palā — homage to your flame! Lay the disease down far away from upon this our man.

sanskrit: kāmas tad agre sam avartata manaso retaḥ prathamaṃ yad āsīt | sa kāma kāmena bṛhatā sayonī rāyaspoṣaṃ yajamānāya dhehi ||
english: Desire came into being at the beginning; that was the first seed of the mind. O Desire, of the same womb as great Desire, grant abundance of wealth to the sacrificer.

sanskrit: tvaṃ kāma sahasāsi pratiṣṭhito vibhur vibhāvā suṣakhā sakhīyate | tvam ugraḥ pṛtanāsu sāsahiḥ saha ojo yajamānāya dhehi ||
english: You, O Desire, are established by force, all-pervading, radiant, a good friend to the one who seeks friendship. You are fierce, ever conquering in battles — grant might and vigour to the sacrificer.

sanskrit: dūrāc cakamānāya pravipāṇāyākṣaye | āsmā aśṛṇvann āśāḥ kāmenājanayan svaḥ ||
english: For the one who desires from afar, for the one who drinks deeply without diminishment — the directions hearkened to him; through Desire they generated the heavenly light.

sanskrit: kāmena mā kāma āgan hṛdayād dhṛdayaṃ pari | yad amīṣām ado manas tad aitūpa mām iha ||
english: By Desire, let Desire come to me, from heart to heart. That yonder mind of those ones — let it come here to me.

sanskrit: yat kāma kāmayamānā idaṃ kṛṇmasi te haviḥ | tan naḥ sarvaṃ sam ṛdhyatām athaitasya haviṣo vīhi svāhā ||
english: O Desire, desiring as we do, this oblation we make for you — let all of that succeed for us! And partake of this oblation — svāhā!

sanskrit: ka idaṃ kasmā adāt kāmaḥ kāmāyādāt | kāmo dātā kāmaḥ pratigrahītā kāmaḥ samudram ā viveśa | kāmena tvā prati gṛhṇāmi kāmaitat te ||
english: Who gave this? To whom was it given? Desire gave it to Desire. Desire is the giver, Desire is the receiver; Desire has entered the ocean. With Desire I receive you — this is your Desire.
